Sweeping in slot order makes that a running total instead: `edge += weight`, one addition, and the weight was needed anyway. The credit walk goes second, and it is the larger of the two. `_creditSlot` repairs all ten ancestors, thirty encrypted additions, once per participant \u2014 rebuilding the same interior sums over and over to add an encrypted zero to everyone who lost. This parks the award on the slot instead and lets the next deposit or withdrawal fold it in, on a path walk that transaction was paying for regardless. What survives is about ten operations a slot: the weight, the two range comparisons, the select, and two additions. Pages are forced to run in order because the running edge only makes sense read left to right. Callers page until `sweepCursor` reaches `slotsUsed`; how many slots fit in one transaction is an HCU question, not a correctness one. Reveals nothing. Free in practice: the callers below all\r\n    /// repair the path immediately afterwards, so this adds one encrypted addition to a\r\n    /// walk that was going to happen regardless.\r\n    ///\r\n    /// Winnings join the balance without earning back-credit for the period \u2014 they were not\r\n    /// staked for the minutes before the draw, so `_lateCredit` is charged for the whole\r\n    /// elapsed part of the period exactly as a fresh deposit would be.\r\n    /// @dev Fold parked winnings in and repair the tree, so they start earning odds.\r\n    ///\r\n    /// Costs nothing at all when there is nothing pending, which is every slot except a\r\n    /// winner's. So the thirty-addition repair is paid once, by the person who won, on a\r\n    /// transaction they were making anyway \u2014 and never by anyone who lost.\r\n    function _settlePending(uint16 slot) internal {\r\n        if (euint64.unwrap(_pendingAward[slot]) == bytes32(0)) return;\r\n\r\n        uint256 node = uint256(LEAF_OFFSET) + slot;\r\n        _foldPending(slot, node);\r\n        _persist(node);\r\n        _repairPath(node);\r\n    }\r\n\r\n    function _foldPending(uint16 slot, uint256 node) private {\r\n        euint64 pending = _pendingAward[slot];\r\n        if (euint64.unwrap(pending) == bytes32(0)) return;\r\n\r\n        _balance[node] = FHE.add(_balance[node], pending);\r\n        _lateCredit[node] = FHE.add(_lateCreditOf(node), FHE.mul(pending, minuteOfPeriod()));\r\n        _pendingAward[slot] = _zero();\r\n    }\r\n\r\n    /// @dev Add encrypted stake to a slot, credited only for the remainder of the period.\r\n    function _creditSlot(uint16 slot, euint64 amount) internal {\r\n        if (slot >= LEAF_COUNT) revert SlotOutOfRange();\r\n\r\n        uint64 m = minuteOfPeriod();\r\n        uint256 node = uint256(LEAF_OFFSET) + slot;\r\n\r\n        _foldPending(slot, node);\r\n        _balance[node] = FHE.add(_balance[node], amount);\r\n        // Full credit would be amount * PERIOD_MINUTES. It only earns from minute `m`\r\n        // onward, so it falls short by exactly `amount * m`.\r\n        _lateCredit[node] = FHE.add(_lateCreditOf(node), FHE.mul(amount, m));\r\n        _earlyExit[node] = _earlyExitOf(node);\r\n        _persist(node);\r\n\r\n        _repairPath(node);\r\n    }\r\n\r\n    /// @dev Remove encrypted stake, keeping the credit it already earned.\r\n    /// @return actual The amount really removed \u2014 clamped to the balance held, because a\r\n    /// ciphertext cannot be compared and branched on, so an over-withdrawal cannot revert.\r\n    function _debitSlot(uint16 slot, euint64 requested) internal returns (euint64 actual) {\r\n        if (slot >= LEAF_COUNT) revert SlotOutOfRange();\r\n\r\n        uint256 node = uint256(LEAF_OFFSET) + slot;\r\n        _foldPending(slot, node);\r\n\r\n        actual = FHE.min(requested, _balance[node]);\r\n        uint64 m = minuteOfPeriod();\r\n\r\n        _balance[node] = FHE.sub(_balance[node], actual);\r\n        // Dropping the balance strips a whole period of credit, but this stake genuinely\r\n        // earned up to minute `m` \u2014 hand that portion back.\r\n        _earlyExit[node] = FHE.add(_earlyExitOf(node), FHE.mul(actual, m));\r\n        _lateCredit[node] = _lateCreditOf(node);\r\n        _persist(node);\r\n\r\n        _repairPath(node);\r\n\r\n        FHE.allowThis(actual);\r\n    }\r\n\r\n    /// @dev The highest node that still covers every slot in use \u2014 the tree's real root.\r\n    ///\r\n    /// A full 1024-leaf tree is ten levels deep, and every credit used to repair all ten.\r\n    /// With twenty depositors that is mostly ceremony: slots 0-19 sit under node 32, and\r\n    /// everything to its right is zero, so node 32 already *equals* node 1. The five levels\r\n    /// above it were being rebuilt on every deposit to copy a number that had not changed.\r\n    ///\r\n    /// So the walk stops here instead, and the depth grows with the pool rather than being\r\n    /// paid for up front. Crossing a power of two moves the root up one level, and the\r\n    /// first credit afterwards computes it \u2014 no migration, no re-indexing.\r\n    ///\r\n    /// Plain arithmetic, no ciphertext: `slotsUsed` is public, and how many people are in\r\n    /// the pool was never a secret.\r\n    function _treeRoot() internal view returns (uint256) {\r\n        uint16 used = slotsUsed;\r\n        if (used <= 1) return LEAF_OFFSET;\r\n\r\n        uint256 span = 1;\r\n        uint256 root = LEAF_OFFSET;\r\n        while (span < used) {\r\n            span <<= 1;\r\n            root >>= 1;\r\n        }\r\n        return root;\r\n    }\r\n\r\n    /// @dev Restore the subtree sums along the ancestors of a leaf, up to {_treeRoot}. Only ancestors can\r\n    /// be affected by a change, which keeps this at 30 encrypted additions rather than a\r\n    /// full re-sum of the tree \u2014 and that bound is what makes the structure viable at all.\r\n    function _repairPath(uint256 node) internal {\r\n        uint256 root = _treeRoot();\r\n        node /= 2;\r\n        while (node >= root) {\r\n            uint256 l = 2 * node;\r\n            uint256 r = l + 1;\r\n\r\n            _balance[node] = FHE.add(_balance[l], _balance[r]);\r\n            _lateCredit[node] = FHE.add(_lateCreditOf(l), _lateCreditOf(r));\r\n            _earlyExit[node] = FHE.add(_earlyExitOf(l), _earlyExitOf(r));\r\n            _persist(node);\r\n\r\n            node /= 2;\r\n        }\r\n    }\r\n\r\n    // -------------------------------------------------------------------------\r\n    // Weights\r\n    // -------------------------------------------------------------------------\r\n\r\n    /// @dev Ticket-minutes under a node. Grouped as (full credit + refunds) - shortfalls so\r\n    /// no intermediate value dips below zero, which unsigned ciphertexts cannot represent.\r\n    function _weightOf(uint256 node) internal returns (euint64) {\r\n        euint64 full = FHE.mul(_balance[node], PERIOD_MINUTES);\r\n        return FHE.sub(FHE.add(full, _earlyExitOf(node)), _lateCreditOf(node));\r\n    }\r\n\r\n    /// @notice Compute your own ticket-minutes and authorise yourself to decrypt them.\r\n    /// @dev A transaction, not a view \u2014 FHE operations mutate coprocessor state. Read the\r\n    /// handle afterwards with {weightHandle} and decrypt it off-chain via EIP-712.\r\n    ///\r\n    /// Restricted to the slot's owner. Without this check anyone could grant themselves\r\n    /// decryption rights over another participant's position.\r\n    function refreshMyWeight() external {\r\n        uint16 slot = slotOf(msg.sender);\r\n        // Winnings must be in the tree before the weight is read, or a winner would see a\r\n        // balance and an odds figure that disagree with each other.\r\n        _settlePending(slot);\r\n\r\n        euint64 w = _weightOf(uint256(LEAF_OFFSET) + slot);\r\n        _weightCache[slot] = w;\r\n        FHE.allowThis(w);\r\n        FHE.allow(w, msg.sender);\r\n    }\r\n\r\n    function weightHandle(uint16 slot) external view returns (euint64) {\r\n        return _weightCache[slot];\r\n    }\r\n\r\n    /// @dev Lets a subclass publish a computed weight through the same handle a reader\r\n    /// already knows to look at.\r\n    function _cacheWeight(uint16 slot, euint64 weight) internal {\r\n        _weightCache[slot] = weight;\r\n    }\r\n\r\n    /// @dev Compute the pool's total ticket-minutes and mark it publicly decryptable.\r\n    ///\r\n    /// Deliberately **internal**. The total is the one aggregate Hushpot publishes, and\r\n    /// only at a draw boundary \u2014 {HushpotPool-openDraw} is the sole caller in production.\r\n    ///\r\n    /// This used to be `external`, which meant anyone could publish the live total on\r\n    /// demand. That is not a small leak: read it, wait for a deposit to land, read it\r\n    /// again, and the difference is that depositor's amount in the clear. Two calls and\r\n    /// the encryption is worth nothing. A subclass exposes it for tests; the pool does\r\n    /// not expose it at all.\r\n    function _refreshTotal() internal {\r\n        euint64 t = _weightOf(_treeRoot());\r\n        _totalCache = t;\r\n        FHE.allowThis(t);\r\n        FHE.makePubliclyDecryptable(t);\r\n    }\r\n\r\n    function totalHandle() external view returns (euint64) {\r\n        return _totalCache;\r\n    }\r\n\r\n    /// @dev For subclasses that need to grant rights over the cached total. Test harnesses\r\n    /// only \u2014 the pool never hands this out.\r\n    function _totalCacheHandle() internal view returns (euint64) {\r\n        return _totalCache;\r\n    }\r\n\r\n    // -------------------------------------------------------------------------\r\n    // Selection\r\n    // -------------------------------------------------------------------------\r\n\r\n    /// @dev Combined ticket-minutes of every slot ordered before this one \u2014 the lower edge\r\n    /// of its band. Climbing from the leaf, a right child's left sibling covers everything\r\n    /// before it, so one addition skips that entire subtree.\r\n    ///\r\n    /// The three components accumulate separately and combine once, so no partial sum can\r\n    /// go negative along the way.\r\n    function _prefixWeight(uint16 slot) internal returns (euint64) {\r\n        euint64 bal = _zero();\r\n        euint64 late = _zero();\r\n        euint64 early = _zero();\r\n\r\n        uint256 node = uint256(LEAF_OFFSET) + slot;\r\n        uint256 root = _treeRoot();\r\n        while (node > root) {\r\n            if (node % 2 == 1) {\r\n                uint256 sib = node - 1;\r\n                bal = FHE.add(bal, _balance[sib]);\r\n                late = FHE.add(late, _lateCreditOf(sib));\r\n                early = FHE.add(early, _earlyExitOf(sib));\r\n            }\r\n            node /= 2;\r\n        }\r\n\r\n        return FHE.sub(FHE.add(FHE.mul(bal, PERIOD_MINUTES), early), late);\r\n    }\r\n\r\n    /// @dev Decide, without revealing anything, whether a slot holds the winning band.\r\n    ///\r\n    /// This is the whole reason Hushpot never learns a winner. The comparison runs on\r\n    /// ciphertext and yields an encrypted boolean the contract cannot read. It is only ever\r\n    /// fed into a `select`, choosing between the prize and zero \u2014 so a loser's claim\r\n    /// silently adds nothing and is indistinguishable on-chain from a winner's.\r\n    function _checkWin(uint16 slot, euint64 drawPoint) internal returns (ebool) {\r\n        if (slot >= LEAF_COUNT) revert SlotOutOfRange();\r\n\r\n        euint64 lower = _prefixWeight(slot);\r\n        euint64 upper = FHE.add(lower, _weightOf(uint256(LEAF_OFFSET) + slot));\r\n\r\n        return FHE.and(FHE.ge(drawPoint, lower), FHE.lt(drawPoint, upper));\r\n    }\r\n}\r\n","keccak256":"0xfe2ab275ea2823c4523db0f631257aa09a669ed69b537e6d086d691edef9fe3e","license":"MIT"},"contracts/HushpotPool.sol":{"content":"// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT\r\npragma solidity ^0.8.27;\r\n\r\nimport {FHE, euint64, ebool, externalEuint64} from \"@fhevm/solidity/lib/FHE.sol\";\r\nimport {IERC20} from \"@openzeppelin/contracts/token/ERC20/IERC20.sol\";\r\nimport {SafeERC20} from \"@openzeppelin/contracts/token/ERC20/utils/SafeERC20.sol\";\r\nimport {Ownable} from \"@openzeppelin/contracts/access/Ownable.sol\";\r\nimport {IERC7984} from \"@openzeppelin/confidential-contracts/interfaces/IERC7984.sol\";\r\n\r\nimport {ConfidentialTimeWeightedTree} from \"./ConfidentialTimeWeightedTree.sol\";\r\n\r\n/// @dev The slice of ERC-7984's ERC-20 wrapper extension the pool needs in order to\r\n/// shield plain tokens on a depositor's behalf. Declared locally so the pool can also be\r\n/// pointed at a non-wrapping confidential token, in which case auto-shielding is simply\r\n/// unavailable and everything else still works.\r\ninterface IConfidentialWrapper {\r\n    function underlying() external view returns (address);\r\n\r\n    function rate() external view returns (uint256);\r\n\r\n    function wrap(address to, uint256 amount) external returns (euint64);\r\n}\r\n\r\n/// @title HushpotPool \u2014 confidential no-loss prize savings\r\n/// @notice Deposit a confidential token, keep your principal, and win the pool's yield.\r\n/// Amounts, balances, odds and the winner all stay encrypted; the draw stays verifiable.\r\n///\r\n/// NO LOSS, STRUCTURALLY\r\n/// ---------------------\r\n/// Deposits and prizes live in separate accounting. A draw never touches principal \u2014 it\r\n/// only ever distributes yield \u2014 so \"withdraw your full deposit whenever you like\" is a\r\n/// property of the design rather than a promise we make.\r\n///\r\n/// GETTING IN\r\n/// ----------\r\n/// The pool moves tokens on your behalf, so it must first be authorised as an operator on\r\n/// the token contract:\r\n///\r\n///     token.setOperator(pool, deadline);\r\n///     pool.deposit(encryptedAmount, proof);\r\n///\r\n/// The amount is encrypted before it leaves the wallet, and the pool learns only a\r\n/// ciphertext handle.\r\n///\r\n/// WHAT LEAKS\r\n/// ----------\r\n/// That a given address deposited, and when \u2014 both are inherent to a public chain, since\r\n/// the transaction itself is visible. Never how much. See `docs/THREAT-MODEL.md`.\r\ncontract HushpotPool is ConfidentialTimeWeightedTree, Ownable {\r\n    using SafeERC20 for IERC20;\r\n\r\n    /// @dev Converts ticket-minutes into a prize at a given annual rate:\r\n    /// `prize = ticketMinutes * annualRateBps / (10_000 * minutesPerYear)`.\r\n    uint256 private constant RATE_DIVISOR = 10_000 * 525_600;\r\n\r\n    struct Draw {\r\n        /// @notice Pool-wide ticket-minutes, published at settlement. The one aggregate\r\n        /// Hushpot ever reveals \u2014 and only here, once a period, never continuously.\r\n        uint64 total;\r\n        /// @notice Prize for this draw. Public, and nobody's balance.\r\n        uint64 prize;\r\n        /// @notice Where the dice landed. Encrypted, and never decrypted by anyone.\r\n        euint64 drawPoint;\r\n        /// @notice The period whose weights this draw was settled against.\r\n        uint32 period;\r\n        bool settled;\r\n    }\r\n\r\n    mapping(uint256 => Draw) public draws;\r\n    uint256 public drawCount;\r\n\r\n    /// @dev Set to true between {openDraw} and {settleDraw}, while the total is out for\r\n    /// decryption.\r\n    bool public drawPending;\r\n    euint64 private _pendingTotal;\r\n\r\n    /// @notice Tokens set aside to pay prizes. Public \u2014 prizes are not anybody's balance.\r\n    uint64 public prizeReserve;\r\n\r\n    /// @notice Annual yield rate in basis points. 500 = 5%.\r\n    /// @dev The prize scales with the pool: a large late depositor grows the pot in\r\n    /// proportion to the odds they take, so nobody can dilute anyone else's expected\r\n    /// return by arriving. See `docs/THREAT-MODEL.md`.\r\n    uint256 public annualRateBps = 500;\r\n\r\n    /// @notice How long a settled draw stays claimable before the period may roll.\r\n    /// @dev Thirty days. A winner who deposits and wanders off for a few weeks still\r\n    /// collects; the old behaviour let the prize evaporate the moment anyone advanced the\r\n    /// period, which could be minutes after settlement.\r\n    uint256 public constant CLAIM_GRACE = 30 days;\r\n\r\n    /// @notice When the most recent draw settled. The claim window runs from here.\r\n    uint256 public lastDrawSettledAt;\r\n\r\n    /// @dev Which slots have already had a given draw evaluated. Public, and it reveals\r\n    /// only that someone was checked \u2014 never whether they won.\r\n    mapping(uint256 => mapping(uint16 => bool)) public claimChecked;\r\n\r\n    event DrawOpened(uint256 indexed drawId, bytes32 totalHandle);\r\n    event DrawSettled(uint256 indexed drawId, uint64 total, uint64 prize);\r\n    event PeriodStarted(uint32 indexed period);\r\n    event ClaimChecked(uint256 indexed drawId, uint16 indexed slot, address indexed checkedBy);\r\n    event ReserveFunded(uint64 amount, uint64 newReserve);\r\n    event PrizeSponsored(address indexed sponsor, uint64 amount);\r\n    event SolvencyProven(uint256 at);\r\n    event RateUpdated(uint256 annualRateBps);\r\n\r\n    error DrawAlreadyPending();\r\n    error DrawAlreadySettledThisPeriod();\r\n    error NoDrawPending();\r\n    error PeriodNotElapsed();\r\n    error ClaimWindowOpen();\r\n    error DrawNotSettled();\r\n    error AlreadyChecked();\r\n    error EmptyPool();\r\n    error PeriodStillOpen();\r\n\r\n    /// @notice The confidential token this pool accepts.\r\n    IERC7984 public immutable token;\r\n\r\n    /// @notice The plain ERC-20 behind {token}, when it is a wrapper. Zero otherwise.\r\n    /// @dev When set, depositors may hand over plain tokens and have the pool shield them,\r\n    /// so nobody has to learn the word \"wrap\".\r\n    IERC20 public immutable underlyingToken;\r\n\r\n    /// @dev Cached principal balances, for the owner to decrypt off-chain.\r\n    mapping(uint16 => euint64) private _balanceCache;\r\n\r\n    event Deposited(address indexed account, uint16 indexed slot);\r\n    event Withdrawn(address indexed account, uint16 indexed slot);\r\n\r\n    /// @dev `amount` is deliberately in the clear \u2014 see {depositUnderlying}.\r\n    event DepositedFromUnderlying(address indexed account, uint16 indexed slot, uint256 amount);\r\n\r\n    error NotAnOperator();\r\n    error NoUnderlyingToken();\r\n    error ZeroAmount();\r\n\r\n    constructor(IERC7984 token_) Ownable(msg.sender) {\r\n        token = token_;\r\n\r\n        // Detect whether this token wraps a plain ERC-20. A confidential token that isn't\r\n        // a wrapper simply reverts here, and auto-shielding stays switched off.\r\n        address found;\r\n        try IConfidentialWrapper(address(token_)).underlying() returns (address u) {\r\n            found = u;\r\n        } catch {\r\n            found = address(0);\r\n        }\r\n        underlyingToken = IERC20(found);\r\n    }\r\n\r\n    /// @notice Whether depositors can hand over plain tokens and be shielded automatically.\r\n    function supportsAutoShield() public view returns (bool) {\r\n        return address(underlyingToken) != address(0);\r\n    }\r\n\r\n    // -------------------------------------------------------------------------\r\n    // Deposit and withdraw\r\n    // -------------------------------------------------------------------------\r\n\r\n    /// @notice Move an encrypted amount into the pool and start earning odds immediately.\r\n    /// @dev Odds accrue from this minute onward, pro-rata for the rest of the period \u2014\r\n    /// there is no waiting period and no lock.\r\n    ///\r\n    /// The tree is credited with the amount the token reports as *actually* transferred,\r\n    /// not the amount requested. ERC-7984 clamps a transfer to the sender's balance rather\r\n    /// than reverting, so crediting the request would let anyone inflate their odds by\r\n    /// asking to deposit more than they hold.\r\n    function deposit(externalEuint64 encryptedAmount, bytes calldata inputProof) external {\r\n        if (!token.isOperator(msg.sender, address(this))) revert NotAnOperator();\r\n\r\n        euint64 requested = FHE.fromExternal(encryptedAmount, inputProof);\r\n        FHE.allowTransient(requested, address(token));\r\n\r\n        euint64 moved = token.confidentialTransferFrom(msg.sender, address(this), requested);\r\n        FHE.allowThis(moved);\r\n\r\n        uint16 slot = _ensureSlot(msg.sender);\r\n        _creditSlot(slot, moved);\r\n\r\n        emit Deposited(msg.sender, slot);\r\n    }\r\n\r\n    /// @notice Deposit plain tokens and let the pool shield them for you.\r\n    /// @dev The convenience path, for anyone holding ordinary tokens rather than\r\n    /// confidential ones. One approval, one call \u2014 no separate wrapping step.\r\n    ///\r\n    /// \u26a0\ufe0f PRIVACY TRADEOFF, AND IT IS REAL. `amount` is a plain number in a plain ERC-20\r\n    /// transfer, so **this deposit's size is public**. Everything afterwards is encrypted \u2014\r\n    /// the position, the odds, the winnings \u2014 but the entry itself is visible.\r\n    ///\r\n    /// Someone who already holds the confidential token should use {deposit} instead,\r\n    /// where the amount never appears in the clear. Anyone wanting both convenience and\r\n    /// privacy can shield at one time and deposit at another, so the two are not linkable\r\n    /// by size or timing. This mirrors the tradeoff in Zama's own confidential vault and\r\n    /// is documented in `docs/THREAT-MODEL.md`.\r\n    function depositUnderlying(uint256 amount) external {\r\n        if (!supportsAutoShield()) revert NoUnderlyingToken();\r\n        if (amount == 0) revert ZeroAmount();\r\n\r\n        underlyingToken.safeTransferFrom(msg.sender, address(this), amount);\r\n        underlyingToken.forceApprove(address(token), amount);\r\n\r\n        // The wrapper mints to us and grants transient access to the caller \u2014 us.\r\n        euint64 minted = IConfidentialWrapper(address(token)).wrap(address(this), amount);\r\n        FHE.allowThis(minted);\r\n\r\n        uint16 slot = _ensureSlot(msg.sender);\r\n        // Credit the amount the wrapper actually minted, not the amount handed over: at a\r\n        // rate above 1 those differ, and any remainder below the rate is not wrapped.\r\n        _creditSlot(slot, minted);\r\n\r\n        emit DepositedFromUnderlying(msg.sender, slot, amount);\r\n    }\r\n\r\n    /// @notice Take principal back out. Any amount, any time, no penalty.\r\n    /// @dev Asking for more than you hold is clamped to your balance rather than reverted,\r\n    /// because a ciphertext cannot be compared and branched on. Either way the caller\r\n    /// receives exactly what they own and never less.\r\n    ///\r\n    /// Odds for the current period keep the credit already earned \u2014 leaving early costs\r\n    /// you the remaining time, not the time you already served.\r\n    function withdraw(externalEuint64 encryptedAmount, bytes calldata inputProof) external {\r\n        uint16 slot = slotOf(msg.sender);\r\n\r\n        euint64 requested = FHE.fromExternal(encryptedAmount, inputProof);\r\n        euint64 actual = _debitSlot(slot, requested);\r\n\r\n        FHE.allowTransient(actual, address(token));\r\n        token.confidentialTransfer(msg.sender, actual);\r\n\r\n        emit Withdrawn(msg.sender, slot);\r\n    }\r\n\r\n    // -------------------------------------------------------------------------\r\n    // Reading your own position\r\n    // -------------------------------------------------------------------------\r\n\r\n    /// @notice Compute your principal and authorise yourself to decrypt it.\r\n    /// @dev A transaction, not a view \u2014 FHE operations mutate coprocessor state. Read the\r\n    /// handle with {balanceHandle} afterwards and decrypt off-chain via EIP-712.\r\n    ///\r\n    /// Only the slot's owner can do this. Without that restriction anyone could grant\r\n    /// themselves decryption rights over someone else's position.\r\n    function refreshMyBalance() external {\r\n        uint16 slot = slotOf(msg.sender);\r\n        _settlePending(slot);\r\n\r\n        euint64 b = _heldBy(slot);\r\n        _balanceCache[slot] = b;\r\n        FHE.allowThis(b);\r\n        FHE.allow(b, msg.sender);\r\n    }\r\n\r\n    function balanceHandle(uint16 slot) external view returns (euint64) {\r\n        return _balanceCache[slot];\r\n    }\r\n\r\n    /// @dev What a slot actually owns: what the tree holds plus anything won and not yet\r\n    /// folded in. The split between the two is an implementation detail of when the\r\n    /// ancestor sums get repaired \u2014 it must never be visible in a balance, or a winner\r\n    /// would check straight after a draw and be told they had lost.\r\n    function _heldBy(uint16 slot) private returns (euint64) {\r\n        euint64 held = _balance[uint256(LEAF_OFFSET) + slot];\r\n        euint64 pending = _pendingAward[slot];\r\n\r\n        return euint64.unwrap(pending) == bytes32(0) ? held : FHE.add(held, pending);\r\n    }\r\n\r\n    /// @notice Recompute your balance and your odds together, in one transaction.\r\n    /// @dev Purely a UX affordance, and a load-bearing one. Reading your own position\r\n    /// needs an on-chain recompute because FHE operations mutate coprocessor state and so\r\n    /// cannot be a free `view` call. Doing balance and weight as separate calls meant three\r\n    /// wallet prompts to answer \"what do I have?\" \u2014 a signature and two transactions.\r\n    /// This collapses it to a signature and one transaction.\r\n    function refreshMyPosition() external {\r\n        uint16 slot = slotOf(msg.sender);\r\n        _settlePending(slot);\r\n        uint256 node = uint256(LEAF_OFFSET) + slot;\r\n\r\n        euint64 b = _heldBy(slot);\r\n        _balanceCache[slot] = b;\r\n        FHE.allowThis(b);\r\n        FHE.allow(b, msg.sender);\r\n\r\n        euint64 w = _weightOf(node);\r\n        _cacheWeight(slot, w);\r\n        FHE.allowThis(w);\r\n        FHE.allow(w, msg.sender);\r\n    }\r\n\r\n    // -------------------------------------------------------------------------\r\n    // Prize reserve\r\n    // -------------------------------------------------------------------------\r\n\r\n    /// @notice Top up the pot. On testnet this stands in for a yield strategy; in\r\n    /// production the same reserve would be fed by real yield. See the README.\r\n    /// @dev Funded with plain tokens on purpose: the amount must be publicly verifiable,\r\n    /// since prizes are public and nobody should have to take our word for the pot size.\r\n    function fundPrizeReserve(uint256 amount) external onlyOwner {\r\n        _fundReserve(amount);\r\n    }\r\n\r\n    /// @notice Grow everyone's prize without taking any odds on it.\r\n    ///\r\n    /// @dev PoolTogether V5 calls this sponsoring: `PrizeVault.sponsor` delegates the\r\n    /// deposit to `SPONSORSHIP_ADDRESS` so it earns yield for the pool but no chance of\r\n    /// winning. Here it is simpler \u2014 a sponsorship goes straight to the shared reserve\r\n    /// and never becomes a slot, so there is no delegation to redirect and no position\r\n    /// to speak of.\r\n    ///\r\n    /// That difference matters. A Code4rena audit of V5 found `sponsor()` could be used\r\n    /// to force *another* account's delegation to the sponsorship address, stripping\r\n    /// their winning chances without consent. Nothing here touches another participant's\r\n    /// slot or weight, so the same mistake is not available to make.\r\n    ///\r\n    /// Deliberately public and in plain tokens: a sponsor is making a claim about the\r\n    /// prize, and a claim about the prize has to be checkable by everyone.\r\n    function sponsorPrize(uint256 amount) external {\r\n        _fundReserve(amount);\r\n        emit PrizeSponsored(msg.sender, uint64(amount / IConfidentialWrapper(address(token)).rate()));\r\n    }\r\n\r\n    function _fundReserve(uint256 amount) private {\r\n        if (!supportsAutoShield()) revert NoUnderlyingToken();\r\n        if (amount == 0) revert ZeroAmount();\r\n\r\n        underlyingToken.safeTransferFrom(msg.sender, address(this), amount);\r\n        underlyingToken.forceApprove(address(token), amount);\r\n        IConfidentialWrapper(address(token)).wrap(address(this), amount);\r\n\r\n        uint64 credited = uint64(amount / IConfidentialWrapper(address(token)).rate());\r\n        prizeReserve += credited;\r\n\r\n        emit ReserveFunded(credited, prizeReserve);\r\n    }\r\n\r\n    /// @notice Set the annual yield rate used to size each prize.\r\n    function setAnnualRateBps(uint256 bps) external onlyOwner {\r\n        require(bps <= 10_000, \"Hushpot: rate above 100%\");\r\n        annualRateBps = bps;\r\n        emit RateUpdated(bps);\r\n    }\r\n\r\n    /// @notice Prize a draw would pay at the given pool size, before the reserve cap.\r\n    /// @dev Deliberately proportional to the pool. Because the pot grows with the deposits\r\n    /// that fund it, a large depositor arriving takes more odds *and* contributes more\r\n    /// prize \u2014 leaving everyone else's expected return exactly unchanged. A fixed pot\r\n    /// would let latecomers extract value from existing depositors.\r\n    function prizeFor(uint64 total) public view returns (uint64) {\r\n        return uint64((uint256(total) * annualRateBps) / RATE_DIVISOR);\r\n    }\r\n\r\n    // -------------------------------------------------------------------------\r\n    // Solvency\r\n    // -------------------------------------------------------------------------\r\n\r\n    /// @notice Encrypted answer to \"is every deposit still backed?\".\r\n    ebool private _fullyBacked;\r\n\r\n    /// @notice When solvency was last proven. Zero if never.\r\n    uint256 public solvencyProvenAt;\r\n\r\n    /// @notice Prove the pool holds at least as much as depositors are owed.\r\n    ///\r\n    /// @dev The obvious objection to a pool whose balances are encrypted is that nobody\r\n    /// can check the money is still there. This answers it without giving anything up:\r\n    /// the comparison runs on ciphertext, and the only thing made public is the single\r\n    /// bit that comes out of it \u2014 backed, or not.\r\n    ///\r\n    /// Neither figure is revealed. Not what the pool holds, not what it owes, and\r\n    /// certainly not any individual position.\r\n    ///\r\n    /// Callable by anyone, deliberately. A solvency proof nobody but the operator can\r\n    /// trigger is not worth much.\r\n    function proveSolvency() external {\r\n        euint64 held = token.confidentialBalanceOf(address(this));\r\n        euint64 owed = _balance[_treeRoot()]; // the tree root is total principal\r\n\r\n        ebool backed = FHE.ge(held, owed);\r\n\r\n        _fullyBacked = backed;\r\n        FHE.allowThis(backed);\r\n        FHE.makePubliclyDecryptable(backed);\r\n        FHE.allow(backed, msg.sender);\r\n\r\n        solvencyProvenAt = block.timestamp;\r\n        emit SolvencyProven(block.timestamp);\r\n    }\r\n\r\n    /// @notice Handle for the last solvency proof. Publicly decryptable \u2014 that is the point.\r\n    function solvencyHandle() external view returns (ebool) {\r\n        return _fullyBacked;\r\n    }\r\n\r\n    // -------------------------------------------------------------------------\r\n    // Draws\r\n    // -------------------------------------------------------------------------\r\n\r\n    /// @notice Whether the current period has run its course.\r\n    function periodEnded() public view returns (bool) {\r\n        return block.timestamp >= periodStart + PERIOD_SECONDS;\r\n    }\r\n\r\n    /// @notice Begin a draw by publishing the pool total for decryption.\r\n    /// @dev Two steps are unavoidable: the draw point must be reduced modulo the pool\r\n    /// total, and encrypted modulo requires a plain divisor. So the total \u2014 the one\r\n    /// aggregate we publish anyway \u2014 is decrypted off-chain and returned with a proof.\r\n    /// The randomness itself never leaves the chain and is never decrypted.\r\n    ///\r\n    /// Anyone may call this once the period has elapsed. The owner may call it early, so\r\n    /// that a draw can be demonstrated without waiting a week.\r\n    function openDraw() external {\r\n        if (drawPending) revert DrawAlreadyPending();\r\n        // One draw per period. Without this, anyone could re-open and re-settle after the\r\n        // period ends and drain the prize reserve a draw at a time.\r\n        if (drawCount > 0 && draws[drawCount - 1].period == currentPeriod) revert DrawAlreadySettledThisPeriod();\r\n        if (!periodEnded() && msg.sender != owner()) revert PeriodNotElapsed();\r\n\r\n        euint64 total = _weightOf(_treeRoot());\r\n        _pendingTotal = total;\r\n        FHE.allowThis(total);\r\n        FHE.makePubliclyDecryptable(total);\r\n        drawPending = true;\r\n\r\n        emit DrawOpened(drawCount, euint64.unwrap(total));\r\n    }\r\n\r\n    function pendingTotalHandle() external view returns (euint64) {\r\n        return _pendingTotal;\r\n    }\r\n\r\n    /// @notice Finish the draw with the decrypted total and its proof.\r\n    /// @dev {FHE.checkSignatures} reverts unless the cleartext genuinely matches the\r\n    /// ciphertext, so whoever relays this cannot lie about the total \u2014 they can only\r\n    /// decline to relay it at all. That is what keeps an off-chain step trustless.\r\n    ///\r\n    /// The draw point is then produced on-chain by the protocol's own generator and\r\n    /// reduced into the pool's range. It stays encrypted forever: no one \u2014 not the caller,\r\n    /// not the owner, not this contract \u2014 ever learns where it landed.\r\n    function settleDraw(bytes calldata abiEncodedCleartexts, bytes calldata decryptionProof) external {\r\n        if (!drawPending) revert NoDrawPending();\r\n\r\n        bytes32[] memory handles = new bytes32[](1);\r\n        handles[0] = euint64.unwrap(_pendingTotal);\r\n        FHE.checkSignatures(handles, abiEncodedCleartexts, decryptionProof);\r\n\r\n        uint64 total = abi.decode(abiEncodedCleartexts, (uint64));\r\n        if (total == 0) revert EmptyPool();\r\n\r\n        uint64 prize = prizeFor(total);\r\n        if (prize > prizeReserve) prize = prizeReserve;\r\n        prizeReserve -= prize;\r\n\r\n        // Uniform over the whole 64-bit range, then folded into [0, total). The residual\r\n        // modulo bias is on the order of total / 2^64 \u2014 far below any observable effect.\r\n        euint64 point = FHE.rem(FHE.randEuint64(), total);\r\n        FHE.allowThis(point);\r\n\r\n        uint256 id = drawCount;\r\n        draws[id] = Draw({total: total, prize: prize, drawPoint: point, period: currentPeriod, settled: true});\r\n        drawCount = id + 1;\r\n        drawPending = false;\r\n        lastDrawSettledAt = block.timestamp;\r\n\r\n        emit DrawSettled(id, total, prize);\r\n    }\r\n\r\n    /// @notice Open the next period, closing the claim window on the last draw.\r\n    ///\r\n    /// @dev Held back for {CLAIM_GRACE} after settlement, and that delay *is* the claim\r\n    /// window.\r\n    ///\r\n    /// A claim recomputes your band from the live tree, which is only sound while the\r\n    /// weights the draw was settled against still stand. They do: once `minuteOfPeriod`\r\n    /// saturates at the end of a period, a deposit adds `amount * PERIOD_MINUTES` to the\r\n    /// balance term and the same to late credit, so it cancels exactly \u2014 and a withdrawal\r\n    /// cancels through early exit the same way. Nothing can move underneath a settled\r\n    /// draw until the period rolls.\r\n    ///\r\n    /// Which means the roll is the only thing that ends a claim, and holding it back costs\r\n    /// nothing at all: no snapshots, no per-slot state, no encrypted work. The price is\r\n    /// paid in cycle length rather than gas \u2014 no draw runs during the grace, and deposits\r\n    /// made in it earn their full credit when the next period opens.\r\n    function startNextPeriod() external {\r\n        if (drawPending) revert DrawAlreadyPending();\r\n        if (drawCount == 0 || draws[drawCount - 1].period != currentPeriod) revert DrawNotSettled();\r\n        if (!periodEnded() && msg.sender != owner()) revert PeriodNotElapsed();\r\n        // The owner may cut the grace short, for the same reason they may open a draw\r\n        // early: a testnet demonstration cannot wait a month to show the second cycle.\r\n        if (block.timestamp < lastDrawSettledAt + CLAIM_GRACE && msg.sender != owner()) revert ClaimWindowOpen();\r\n\r\n        _advancePeriod();\r\n        emit PeriodStarted(currentPeriod);\r\n    }\r\n\r\n    // -------------------------------------------------------------------------\r\n    // Claims\r\n    // -------------------------------------------------------------------------\r\n\r\n    /// @notice Evaluate a draw for one participant and pay them if they won.\r\n    ///\r\n    /// @dev Deliberately callable by anyone, for anyone. The result is encrypted either\r\n    /// way, so the caller learns nothing \u2014 which means a keeper can sweep every\r\n    /// participant after each draw and the prize simply *appears* in the winner's balance.\r\n    /// Nobody has to remember to check, and because everyone gets checked, the fact that\r\n    /// someone was checked says nothing about whether they won.\r\n    ///\r\n    /// A loser's claim adds an encrypted zero. On-chain it is indistinguishable from the\r\n    /// winner's, down to the gas.\r\n    ///\r\n    /// Safe to run while the period is over but not yet rolled: once `minuteOfPeriod`\r\n    /// saturates, deposits and withdrawals cancel out of the weight arithmetic exactly, so\r\n    /// the numbers this draw was settled against cannot move underneath it.\r\n    function checkClaim(uint256 drawId, address account) public {\r\n        Draw storage d = draws[drawId];\r\n        if (!d.settled) revert DrawNotSettled();\r\n        if (d.period != currentPeriod) revert AlreadyChecked();\r\n\r\n        uint16 slot = slotOf(account);\r\n        if (claimChecked[drawId][slot]) revert AlreadyChecked();\r\n        claimChecked[drawId][slot] = true;\r\n\r\n        ebool won = _checkWin(slot, d.drawPoint);\r\n        euint64 award = FHE.select(won, FHE.asEuint64(d.prize), FHE.asEuint64(0));\r\n\r\n        // Parked, not credited. Crediting repairs all ten ancestor sums \u2014 thirty encrypted\r\n        // additions \u2014 to deposit what is, for all but one checker, an encrypted zero. The\r\n        // award joins the tree on this slot's next deposit or withdrawal, which walks that\r\n        // path anyway. Winnings still join the principal, just one transaction later.\r\n        _pendingAward[slot] = FHE.add(_pendingAward[slot], award);\r\n        FHE.allowThis(_pendingAward[slot]);\r\n\r\n        emit ClaimChecked(drawId, slot, msg.sender);\r\n    }\r\n\r\n    /// @notice Check a draw for a handful of participants in one transaction.\r\n    ///\r\n    /// @dev \u26a0\ufe0f Not a whole-pool sweep, despite the shape. A single claim is roughly 60\u201380\r\n    /// encrypted operations \u2014 the prefix walk, the range comparison, the select and the\r\n    /// credit \u2014 so only about one or two fit inside the per-transaction HCU ceiling.\r\n    /// Measured on Sepolia: ~2.4M gas each, and five together revert.\r\n    ///\r\n    /// A keeper should therefore page through participants with one transaction each\r\n    /// rather than calling this with a long list. `hushpot:sweep` does exactly that.\r\n    /// This exists for the small-batch case and to keep the loop skip-safe.\r\n    ///\r\n    /// Skips anyone already checked, so it is safe to re-run.\r\n    function checkClaimBatch(uint256 drawId, address[] calldata accounts) external {\r\n        for (uint256 i = 0; i < accounts.length; i++) {\r\n            address account = accounts[i];\r\n            if (!hasSlot(account)) continue;\r\n            if (claimChecked[drawId][slotOf(account)]) continue;\r\n            checkClaim(drawId, account);\r\n        }\r\n    }\r\n\r\n    /// @dev Running lower edge of the band, carried between pages of a sweep.\r\n    mapping(uint256 => euint64) private _sweepEdge;\r\n\r\n    /// @notice Next slot a sweep of this draw will process. Equal to `slotsUsed` when done.\r\n    mapping(uint256 => uint16) public sweepCursor;\r\n\r\n    error SweepOutOfOrder();\r\n\r\n    /// @notice Pay out a draw across a range of slots in one transaction.\r\n    ///\r\n    /// @dev This is the cheap way to settle a draw, and the reason is structural rather than\r\n    /// clever: a per-participant claim repeats work that is identical for everybody.\r\n    ///\r\n    /// Two costs disappear here.\r\n    ///\r\n    /// The prefix walk goes first. A lone claim climbs the tree to rederive the combined\r\n    /// weight of everyone ordered before it \u2014 three additions per set bit of the slot index.\r\n    /// Sweeping in slot order makes that a running total instead: `edge += weight`, one\r\n    /// addition, and the weight was needed anyway.\r\n    ///\r\n    /// The credit walk goes second, and it is the larger of the two. `_creditSlot` repairs\r\n    /// all ten ancestors, thirty encrypted additions, once per participant \u2014 rebuilding the\r\n    /// same interior sums over and over to add an encrypted zero to everyone who lost. This\r\n    /// parks the award on the slot instead and lets the next deposit or withdrawal fold it\r\n    /// in, on a path walk that transaction was paying for regardless.\r\n    ///\r\n    /// What survives is about ten operations a slot: the weight, the two range comparisons,\r\n    /// the select, and two additions.\r\n    ///\r\n    /// Pages are forced to run in order because the running edge only makes sense read\r\n    /// left to right. Callers page until `sweepCursor` reaches `slotsUsed`; how many slots\r\n    /// fit in one transaction is an HCU question, not a correctness one.\r\n    ///\r\n    /// Reveals nothing. Every slot in the range is treated identically, the award is\r\n    /// `select(won, prize, 0)` for all of them, and the losers' encrypted zeros are\r\n    /// indistinguishable from the winner's prize.\r\n    function sweepRange(uint256 drawId, uint16 count) external {\r\n        Draw storage d = draws[drawId];\r\n        if (!d.settled) revert DrawNotSettled();\r\n        if (d.period != currentPeriod) revert AlreadyChecked();\r\n\r\n        uint16 from = sweepCursor[drawId];\r\n        if (from >= slotsUsed) revert SweepOutOfOrder();\r\n\r\n        uint16 to = from + count;\r\n        if (to > slotsUsed) to = slotsUsed;\r\n\r\n        euint64 edge = from == 0 ? _zero() : _sweepEdge[drawId];\r\n\r\n        for (uint16 slot = from; slot < to; slot++) {\r\n            edge = _sweepSlot(drawId, slot, edge);\r\n        }\r\n\r\n        _sweepEdge[drawId] = edge;\r\n        FHE.allowThis(edge);\r\n        sweepCursor[drawId] = to;\r\n    }\r\n\r\n    /// @dev One slot of a sweep. Split out only because the loop ran the stack out of depth.\r\n    /// @return upper The band's upper edge, which is the next slot's lower edge.\r\n    function _sweepSlot(uint256 drawId, uint16 slot, euint64 edge) private returns (euint64 upper) {\n        Draw storage d = draws[drawId];\n\n        upper = FHE.add(edge, _weightOf(uint256(LEAF_OFFSET) + slot));\n        if (claimChecked[drawId][slot]) return upper;\n\n        euint64 award = FHE.select(\n            FHE.and(FHE.ge(d.drawPoint, edge), FHE.lt(d.drawPoint, upper)),\n            FHE.asEuint64(d.prize),\n            FHE.asEuint64(0)\n        );\r\n\r\n        _pendingAward[slot] = FHE.add(_pendingAward[slot], award);\r\n        FHE.allowThis(_pendingAward[slot]);\r\n\r\n        claimChecked[drawId][slot] = true;\r\n        emit ClaimChecked(drawId, slot, msg.sender);\r\n    }\r\n}\r\n","keccak256":"0x88b7a50fa8d0a72cebc69129dfdb8b02870f436abeebfcfe130c93221eedd658","license":"MIT"},"encrypted-types/EncryptedTypes.sol":{"content":"// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT\npragma OwnableInvalidOwner(address).details: The owner is not a valid owner account. (eg. `address(0)`)

OwnableUnauthorizedAccount(address).details: The caller account is not authorized to perform an operation.

SafeERC20FailedOperation(address).details: An operation with an ERC-20 token failed.

DepositedFromUnderlying(address,uint16,u.details: `amount` is deliberately in the clear — see {depositUnderlying}.

checkClaim(uint256,address).details: Deliberately callable by anyone, for anyone. The result is encrypted either way, so the caller learns nothing — which means a keeper can sweep every participant after each draw and the prize simply *appears* in the winner's balance. Nobody has to remember to check, and because everyone gets checked, the fact that someone was checked says nothing about whether they won. A loser's claim adds an encrypted zero. On-chain it is indistinguishable from the winner's, down to the gas. Safe to run while the period is over but not yet rolled: once `minuteOfPeriod` saturates, deposits and withdrawals cancel out of the weight arithmetic exactly, so the numbers this draw was settled against cannot move underneath it.

checkClaimBatch(uint256,address[]).details: ⚠️ Not a whole-pool sweep, despite the shape. A single claim is roughly 60–80 encrypted operations — the prefix walk, the range comparison, the select and the credit — so only about one or two fit inside the per-transaction HCU ceiling. Measured on Sepolia: ~2.4M gas each, and five together revert. A keeper should therefore page through participants with one transaction each rather than calling this with a long list. `hushpot:sweep` does exactly that. This exists for the small-batch case and to keep the loop skip-safe. Skips anyone already checked, so it is safe to re-run.

deposit(bytes32,bytes).details: Odds accrue from this minute onward, pro-rata for the rest of the period — there is no waiting period and no lock. The tree is credited with the amount the token reports as *actually* transferred, not the amount requested. ERC-7984 clamps a transfer to the sender's balance rather than reverting, so crediting the request would let anyone inflate their odds by asking to deposit more than they hold.

depositUnderlying(uint256).details: The convenience path, for anyone holding ordinary tokens rather than confidential ones. One approval, one call — no separate wrapping step. ⚠️ PRIVACY TRADEOFF, AND IT IS REAL. `amount` is a plain number in a plain ERC-20 transfer, so **this deposit's size is public**. Everything afterwards is encrypted — the position, the odds, the winnings — but the entry itself is visible. Someone who already holds the confidential token should use {deposit} instead, where the amount never appears in the clear. Anyone wanting both convenience and privacy can shield at one time and deposit at another, so the two are not linkable by size or timing. This mirrors the tradeoff in Zama's own confidential vault and is documented in `docs/THREAT-MODEL.md`.

fundPrizeReserve(uint256).details: Funded with plain tokens on purpose: the amount must be publicly verifiable, since prizes are public and nobody should have to take our word for the pot size.

openDraw().details: Two steps are unavoidable: the draw point must be reduced modulo the pool total, and encrypted modulo requires a plain divisor. So the total — the one aggregate we publish anyway — is decrypted off-chain and returned with a proof. The randomness itself never leaves the chain and is never decrypted. Anyone may call this once the period has elapsed. The owner may call it early, so that a draw can be demonstrated without waiting a week.

owner().details: Returns the address of the current owner.

prizeFor(uint64).details: Deliberately proportional to the pool. Because the pot grows with the deposits that fund it, a large depositor arriving takes more odds *and* contributes more prize — leaving everyone else's expected return exactly unchanged. A fixed pot would let latecomers extract value from existing depositors.

proveSolvency().details: The obvious objection to a pool whose balances are encrypted is that nobody can check the money is still there. This answers it without giving anything up: the comparison runs on ciphertext, and the only thing made public is the single bit that comes out of it — backed, or not. Neither figure is revealed. Not what the pool holds, not what it owes, and certainly not any individual position. Callable by anyone, deliberately. A solvency proof nobody but the operator can trigger is not worth much.

refreshMyBalance().details: A transaction, not a view — FHE operations mutate coprocessor state. Read the handle with {balanceHandle} afterwards and decrypt off-chain via EIP-712. Only the slot's owner can do this. Without that restriction anyone could grant themselves decryption rights over someone else's position.

refreshMyPosition().details: Purely a UX affordance, and a load-bearing one. Reading your own position needs an on-chain recompute because FHE operations mutate coprocessor state and so cannot be a free `view` call. Doing balance and weight as separate calls meant three wallet prompts to answer "what do I have?" — a signature and two transactions. This collapses it to a signature and one transaction.

refreshMyWeight().details: A transaction, not a view — FHE operations mutate coprocessor state. Read the handle afterwards with {weightHandle} and decrypt it off-chain via EIP-712. Restricted to the slot's owner. Without this check anyone could grant themselves decryption rights over another participant's position.

renounceOwnership().details: Leaves the contract without owner. It will not be possible to call `onlyOwner` functions. Can only be called by the current owner. NOTE: Renouncing ownership will leave the contract without an owner, thereby disabling any functionality that is only available to the owner.

settleDraw(bytes,bytes).details: {FHE.checkSignatures} reverts unless the cleartext genuinely matches the ciphertext, so whoever relays this cannot lie about the total — they can only decline to relay it at all. That is what keeps an off-chain step trustless. The draw point is then produced on-chain by the protocol's own generator and reduced into the pool's range. It stays encrypted forever: no one — not the caller, not the owner, not this contract — ever learns where it landed.

sponsorPrize(uint256).details: PoolTogether V5 calls this sponsoring: `PrizeVault.sponsor` delegates the deposit to `SPONSORSHIP_ADDRESS` so it earns yield for the pool but no chance of winning. Here it is simpler — a sponsorship goes straight to the shared reserve and never becomes a slot, so there is no delegation to redirect and no position to speak of. That difference matters. A Code4rena audit of V5 found `sponsor()` could be used to force *another* account's delegation to the sponsorship address, stripping their winning chances without consent. Nothing here touches another participant's slot or weight, so the same mistake is not available to make. Deliberately public and in plain tokens: a sponsor is making a claim about the prize, and a claim about the prize has to be checkable by everyone.

startNextPeriod().details: Held back for {CLAIM_GRACE} after settlement, and that delay *is* the claim window. A claim recomputes your band from the live tree, which is only sound while the weights the draw was settled against still stand. They do: once `minuteOfPeriod` saturates at the end of a period, a deposit adds `amount * PERIOD_MINUTES` to the balance term and the same to late credit, so it cancels exactly — and a withdrawal cancels through early exit the same way. Nothing can move underneath a settled draw until the period rolls. Which means the roll is the only thing that ends a claim, and holding it back costs nothing at all: no snapshots, no per-slot state, no encrypted work. The price is paid in cycle length rather than gas — no draw runs during the grace, and deposits made in it earn their full credit when the next period opens.

sweepRange(uint256,uint16).details: This is the cheap way to settle a draw, and the reason is structural rather than clever: a per-participant claim repeats work that is identical for everybody. Two costs disappear here. The prefix walk goes first. A lone claim climbs the tree to rederive the combined weight of everyone ordered before it — three additions per set bit of the slot index. Sweeping in slot order makes that a running total instead: `edge += weight`, one addition, and the weight was needed anyway. The credit walk goes second, and it is the larger of the two. `_creditSlot` repairs all ten ancestors, thirty encrypted additions, once per participant — rebuilding the same interior sums over and over to add an encrypted zero to everyone who lost. This parks the award on the slot instead and lets the next deposit or withdrawal fold it in, on a path walk that transaction was paying for regardless. What survives is about ten operations a slot: the weight, the two range comparisons, the select, and two additions. Pages are forced to run in order because the running edge only makes sense read left to right. Callers page until `sweepCursor` reaches `slotsUsed`; how many slots fit in one transaction is an HCU question, not a correctness one. Reveals nothing. Every slot in the range is treated identically, the award is `select(won, prize, 0)` for all of them, and the losers' encrypted zeros are indistinguishable from the winner's prize.

transferOwnership(address).details: Transfers ownership of the contract to a new account (`newOwner`). Can only be called by the current owner.

withdraw(bytes32,bytes).details: Asking for more than you hold is clamped to your balance rather than reverted, because a ciphertext cannot be compared and branched on. Either way the caller receives exactly what they own and never less. Odds for the current period keep the credit already earned — leaving early costs you the remaining time, not the time you already served.

CLAIM_GRACE.details: Thirty days. A winner who deposits and wanders off for a few weeks still collects; the old behaviour let the prize evaporate the moment anyone advanced the period, which could be minutes after settlement.

RATE_DIVISOR.details: Converts ticket-minutes into a prize at a given annual rate: `prize = ticketMinutes * annualRateBps / (10_000 * minutesPerYear)`.

_balanceCache.details: Cached principal balances, for the owner to decrypt off-chain.

_sweepEdge.details: Running lower edge of the band, carried between pages of a sweep.

annualRateBps.details: The prize scales with the pool: a large late depositor grows the pot in proportion to the odds they take, so nobody can dilute anyone else's expected return by arriving. See `docs/THREAT-MODEL.md`.

claimChecked.details: Which slots have already had a given draw evaluated. Public, and it reveals only that someone was checked — never whether they won.

drawPending.details: Set to true between {openDraw} and {settleDraw}, while the total is out for decryption.

underlyingToken.details: When set, depositors may hand over plain tokens and have the pool shield them, so nobody has to learn the word "wrap".

InvalidKMSSignatures().notice: Returned if the returned KMS signatures are not valid.

SenderNotAllowedToUseHandle(bytes32,addr.notice: Returned if the sender is not allowed to use the handle.

ZamaProtocolUnsupported().notice: Returned if the Zama protocol is not supported on the current chain

PublicDecryptionVerified(bytes32[],bytes.notice: This event is emitted when public decryption has been successfully verified.

CLAIM_GRACE().notice: How long a settled draw stays claimable before the period may roll.

PERIOD_MINUTES().notice: One draw period, in minutes. One week.

annualRateBps().notice: Annual yield rate in basis points. 500 = 5%.

checkClaim(uint256,address).notice: Evaluate a draw for one participant and pay them if they won.

checkClaimBatch(uint256,address[]).notice: Check a draw for a handful of participants in one transaction.

deposit(bytes32,bytes).notice: Move an encrypted amount into the pool and start earning odds immediately.

depositUnderlying(uint256).notice: Deposit plain tokens and let the pool shield them for you.

fundPrizeReserve(uint256).notice: Top up the pot. On testnet this stands in for a yield strategy; in production the same reserve would be fed by real yield. See the README.

lastDrawSettledAt().notice: When the most recent draw settled. The claim window runs from here.

minuteOfPeriod().notice: Minutes elapsed in the current period, saturating at the period length.

openDraw().notice: Begin a draw by publishing the pool total for decryption.

periodEnded().notice: Whether the current period has run its course.

prizeFor(uint64).notice: Prize a draw would pay at the given pool size, before the reserve cap.

prizeReserve().notice: Tokens set aside to pay prizes. Public — prizes are not anybody's balance.

proveSolvency().notice: Prove the pool holds at least as much as depositors are owed.

refreshMyBalance().notice: Compute your principal and authorise yourself to decrypt it.

refreshMyPosition().notice: Recompute your balance and your odds together, in one transaction.

refreshMyWeight().notice: Compute your own ticket-minutes and authorise yourself to decrypt them.

setAnnualRateBps(uint256).notice: Set the annual yield rate used to size each prize.

settleDraw(bytes,bytes).notice: Finish the draw with the decrypted total and its proof.

slotOf(address).notice: The slot held by `account`, or reverts if they have never deposited.

solvencyHandle().notice: Handle for the last solvency proof. Publicly decryptable — that is the point.

solvencyProvenAt().notice: When solvency was last proven. Zero if never.

sponsorPrize(uint256).notice: Grow everyone's prize without taking any odds on it.

startNextPeriod().notice: Open the next period, closing the claim window on the last draw.

supportsAutoShield().notice: Whether depositors can hand over plain tokens and be shielded automatically.

sweepCursor(uint256).notice: Next slot a sweep of this draw will process. Equal to `slotsUsed` when done.

sweepRange(uint256,uint16).notice: Pay out a draw across a range of slots in one transaction.

token().notice: The confidential token this pool accepts.

underlyingToken().notice: The plain ERC-20 behind {token}, when it is a wrapper. Zero otherwise.

withdraw(bytes32,bytes).notice: Take principal back out. Any amount, any time, no penalty.

userdoc.notice: Deposit a confidential token, keep your principal, and win the pool's yield. Amounts, balances, odds and the winner all stay encrypted; the draw stays verifiable. NO LOSS, STRUCTURALLY --------------------- Deposits and prizes live in separate accounting. A draw never touches principal — it only ever distributes yield — so "withdraw your full deposit whenever you like" is a property of the design rather than a promise we make. GETTING IN ---------- The pool moves tokens on your behalf, so it must first be authorised as an operator on the token contract:     token.setOperator(pool, deadline);     pool.deposit(encryptedAmount, proof); The amount is encrypted before it leaves the wallet, and the pool learns only a ciphertext handle. WHAT LEAKS ---------- That a given address deposited, and when — both are inherent to a public chain, since the transaction itself is visible. Never how much. See `docs/THREAT-MODEL.md`.
